what_it_states: Exploratory, experimental study restricted to scalar (one-dimensional numeric) queries and oblivious noise-generation mechanisms under pure epsilon-DP (alpha = e^{-epsilon}); background after Ghosh-Roughgarden-Sundararajan: Bayesian (OPT1) and risk-averse minimax (OPT2) expected-loss formulations for countable ranges; reviews Laplacian, Geometric and Staircase mechanisms (staircase gamma set to the one-dimensional minimizer of expected noise amplitude); open questions R1 (universally optimal oblivious mechanisms beyond Brenner-Nissim), R2 (optimal mechanism without constant sensitivity), R3 (optimal scalar mechanism in the Bayesian model with side information). Section 5: normalized expected |x|-loss comparisons for mean, max and count queries; a two-stage heuristic (pre-rounding to {-10,0,10} plus generalized Geometric noise) reported to improve expected loss in the low-medium privacy regime under side information; Lemma 1 (for Laplacian, Staircase and Geometric noise with loss |i-j|, the MLE collusion strategy is the sample median, proof in the Appendix); large-k approximations of collusion expected loss decaying like 1/sqrt(k). Conclusion: the paper is focused on one-dimensional numeric queries; it conjectures that a heuristic mechanism betters Staircase and Laplace under side information; future work includes optimal mechanisms in the multi-dimensional query output scenario.
what_it_does_not_state: No planar, R^2 or l1-diamond model; no theorem on multi-dimensional optimal noise (multi-dimensional design is listed as future work only); no all-law optimum in any dimension; no squared-Euclidean MSE optimum or selector in dimension two; no mixed-cost all-law bound E||Z||_2^2 >= (2/3) inf E||Z||_1^2 or its equality case; no rounded-core selector.
registered_planar_result_explicitly_stat: NO (neither the planar mixed-cost bound nor the planar all-law MSE result is explicitly stated in the 336 retained logical lines).
